Every number on this page is computed from the JSON baselines committed under `bench/baselines/`
when the site is built (`site/gen_pages.py`). None is typed by hand.

{{< include _results-meta.md >}}

## Correctness

- **Golden fronts.** `zeno` reproduces all 27 fronts of the brute-force oracle
  ([golden suite](instances/suites.qmd#golden)). Five of them are instances on which the 2016
  solvers were still wrong after their bookkeeping fixes, because their greedy schedule is not
  optimal ([§5](proofs.qmd#node-s5)).
- **Every level.** `ut-zeno-core` compares the value of every level, the bracket order
  $L \le E \le U_3 \le U$ and the front with an independent enumeration oracle on random instances.
- **Non-symmetric.** On 1,800 tiny random non-symmetric instances, every bracket closes and equals
  the oracle's front.
- **Two solvers, one front.** The Lean solver `zeno-front`, whose output is proved to be the front,
  gives the same front as `zeno front` on every suite instance (table below). CI compares the two on
  the golden, quick and three regime instances.
- **Certificates.** CI writes certificates for the golden and random instances with `zeno` and has
  both checkers verify them. The Lean checker accepts the certificates of all 66 suite instances.

The 2016 solvers (`zenoSolver`, `zenoSolver_naive`, `zenoSolver_noDuplicate`) were removed from
the code; their baselines are kept for comparison, and commit `84ca92a` still builds them. Their
fronts are those of the legacy greedy, wrong on some instances, so their front sizes are not a
reference.

### Per instance

Front size and `zeno` time from `zeno.json` (median of 3 runs, all cores); 2016 `zenoSolver`
(median of 3, 30 s timeout); Lean `zeno-front` (one run, 60 s timeout, "differs" if its front is
not `zeno front`'s); Lean `zeno-check` on the certificate `zeno` writes, and that certificate's
size.

## Time against the level range

The `sqrt` family on $n = 10$, $t = 8$, $p = 3$ with durations scaled by `-r`
(`BM_SolveLargeDurations`, median of 3 runs). The number of levels grows linearly with `-r`. The
number of levels the breakpoint search evaluates, and the time, grow only with its logarithm:

## The Lean checker

{{< include _results-checker.md >}}

The `rejected/` certificates of the test set are corrupted on purpose, so their rejection is the
expected verdict. The one rejected random version 2 certificate is the
[Proposition 6.5](proofs.qmd#node-proposition-6-5) instance (`v2-random/prop65`); `bench/README.md`
notes that it needs the `search` kind. The certificate `zeno` writes today for that instance closes
two gaps with `search`, and `zeno-check` accepts it ([Lean tools](solver/lean.qmd#zeno-check)).

## Component benchmarks and CI {#ci}

Each algorithm component has a Google Benchmark executable (`bm-core`, `bm-plan`, `bm-ns`), with
counters that explain its time (peak RSS, states, gap levels, certificate bytes) and complexity fits
to compare with the bounds of the note. Their baselines are in `bench/baselines/zeno/<machine>/`,
recorded while other builds ran, so differences below 20% are noise.

`.github/workflows/bench.yml` runs every component benchmark and the `quick` suite on pull requests
and writes the comparison with `bench/baselines/*/ci-ubuntu-24.04/` to the job summary, without
blocking. A nightly run on the runner named by `ZS_BENCH_RUNNER` fails on a regression above
`ZS_BENCH_THRESHOLD` (default 25%, with a 5 ms noise floor). See
[`bench/README.md`](https://github.com/aquemy/ZenoSolver/blob/master/bench/README.md) for the tools
and the baseline layout.
